author: Julian Macfarlane
title: Both sides now: proxy wars
text:
Ukraine is a US and NATO proxy setup to conduct unprovoked full-scale war against Russia, initially by attacking Russian people in Donbass and Lugansk and Odessa.
In 2022 NATO had equipped Ukrainian armies creating the largest military force in Europe at the time for a “final solution” to kill or drive out Russian speaking Ukrainians in southern and eastern Ukraine, an effort which had begun in 2014 when the neo-Nazis overthrew the legally and democratically elected government of Ukraine.
The Russians call this war a "Special Military Operation" because it is not a war against Ukraine but rather a defensive operation against the Russophobic nations of Europe and the Anglosphere. Now of course the Americans are pretending that the war is Ukraine’s, despite providing intelligence and targeting information to Ukraine as well as weapons to US allies in Europe who provide those same weapons to Kyiv, although they get blown up on arrival for the most part.
The hypocrisy is obvious. But this is the American way of war since Vietnam.
It does not fight wars American-style in large numbers anymore, not when it can bribe corrupt elites in foreign countries to send their people to die for the Stars & Stripes.
However, as a result of this craven strategy, Ukraine has become a battlefield where Russia must defend against NATO and the US.
Of course, Russia knows who it’s real enemies are. Not the people of Ukraine, but the Western powers who have schemed the downfall of Russia for centuries.
While Americans are not dying in any number in Ukraine, Russians are – even if their casualty rate is now 30 times lower than that of the Ukrainians who have lost well over 2 million, an enormous number for country now with only 20 to 30 million people left. Demographically it is a disaster.
This is a very long slow war. Partly because the Russians want to keep their casualties as low as possible and prevent civilian casualties in the battlefield areas , as well as to prevent damaging casualties in the rear areas of Russia itself. Also, partly because the longer the war goes on the more it wears down Europe and the US in all areas – socially, politically, economically, and militarily. Russia is destroying the West. In addition, the longer the war goes on the more unified Russia becomes as a civilization, the more self-evident its values, the more pressure there is for its economy and industry to adapt and grow, and the more capable its military. This is an existential war and existential wars drive growth.
In 2022, for example, the Russian military was still using a lot of Soviet era equipment, especially in the case of its naval forces and in land warfare as well – it was not prepared for drone warfare or cruise missiles or the like.
In the first two weeks, Russia lost a lot of tanks and aircraft before it changed his tactics, which to its credit it did very quickly.
After that, however, it found it difficult to control the Black Sea with its naval assets which were designed for a different kind of war and should have been scrapped years before.
Now, it has changed its tactics, targeting Ukrainian commercial vessels using airpower. At the same time however, it must adapt to attacks on its merchant fleet as well as to drone attacks on civilian centers and industrial infrastructure. Russia may shoot down 95% of drones and cruise missiles launched at it but there always a few that get through. So it is developing advanced technology to counter the threats.
Russia therefore continues to adapt. It has to because this is a practice session for a real war with the West in the future. It has developed new and state-of-the-art drone, glide bomb, cruise missile, hypersonic technologies, which are far superior to anything that the West has. It is developing new and technologically unrivaled naval technologies, emphasizing submarines with an innovative range of weapons, which the West cannot match and cannot defend against.
The US recently acknowledged putting weapons in space, but the Russians anticipated this long ago and are prepared with their own space weapons, and also ground-based antisatellite and antimissile systems like the S500.
The Russian Federation's nuclear weaponry is now far in advance of the West – not that anyone contemplates a nuclear war. If Europe goes to war with Russia, it will not be nuclear, but it will be over very quickly, probably in just a few weeks, with NATO bases across Europe destroyed, along with factories, command centers and the like.
Yet, while the Russian military is growing and developing at an unprecedented pace the Kremlin feels it is not yet ready for all out war.
It recognizes however that the West only understands force. In this sense, the Ukrainian SMO has been helpful as a demonstration.
Add to that the lessons of the US war with Iran. Iran hasn’t won the war militarily but hasn’t lost it either and it has demonstrated the vulnerability of US military technologies as well as the economic consequences of war with resource rich countries. Economically Iran is winning.
